div.b: Why the two-key split is the whole point

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 611px; margin-left: 989px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10.5px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
Without the gateway
Every app holds a live provider key. The key is
in env files, images, and laptops. You cannot
tell which team spent what. Revoking one key
breaks every app sharing it. Any model the
provider offers is reachable.
With the gateway
• The provider key is entered once and is
never distributed.
• Each app gets its own gateway key, so it
can be revoked alone.
• Every call is attributable, because the key
identifies the caller.
• Rotating the provider key is one edit in
SCM, with no application change.
• Budget, rate, and model limits attach to
the key, not to the provider account.
